signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.completion_factor_mono {q k s : ℝ} (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hqk : q ≤ k) (hks : k < s - 1) :
  q / (s - q - 1) ≤ k / (s - k - 1)
name: NLAlib.Assembly.completion_factor_mono
doc:
Monotonicity of the completion factor (Chen–Persson, proof of `thm:GN`): `q ↦ q/(s−q−1)`
is increasing for `q < s − 1`, so the factor of `lem:completion` for dimension `q ≤ k` is at
most that for `k`. Helper for atlas `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.gn_assembly.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {X Y cfac : Ω → ℝ}
  {cmax B : ℝ} (hY : 0 ≤ Y) (hcmax : 0 ≤ cmax) (hc : ∀ (ω : Ω), cfac ω ≤ cmax)
  (hcond : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = ∫ (ω : Ω), cfac ω * Y ω ∂μ) (hYbound : ∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ ≤ B)
  (hcYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => cfac ω * Y ω) μ) (hYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Y μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ cmax * B
name: NLAlib.Assembly.gn_assembly
doc:
Abstract assembly of Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN` (Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1).
* `X = ‖A − Â‖_F²`, `Y = ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²` (the range-finder error),
  `cfac ω = 1 + q(ω)/(s − q(ω) − 1)` with `q = rank(AΩ)` the (random) number of columns of `Q`.
* `hcond` encodes `lem:completion` after the tower property (conditioning on `Ω`, using
  independence of `Ψ` and `Ω`): `E X = E[(1 + q/(s−q−1)) Y]`.
* `hc` is the deterministic bound `q ≤ t` and monotonicity of `q ↦ q/(s−q−1)`
  (`completion_factor_mono`).
* `hYbound` is the range-finder theorem (`thm:RSVD`).
Atlas `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.gn_explicit.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X Y cfac Zsq : Ω → ℝ} {k t s OPTsq : ℝ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hkt : k + 2 ≤ t)
  (hts : t + 2 ≤ s) (hY : 0 ≤ Y) (hc : ∀ (ω : Ω), cfac ω ≤ 1 + t / (s - t - 1))
  (hcond : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = ∫ (ω : Ω), cfac ω * Y ω ∂μ) (hstruct : ∀ (ω : Ω), Y ω ≤ OPTsq + Zsq ω)
  (hZ : ∫ (ω : Ω), Zsq ω ∂μ = k / (t - k - 1) * OPTsq) (hcYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => cfac ω * Y ω) μ)
  (hYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Y μ) (hZi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Zsq μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ (1 + t / (s - t - 1)) * ((1 + k / (t - k - 1)) * OPTsq)
name: NLAlib.Assembly.gn_explicit
doc:
Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN` (Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1), expectation level:
`t ≥ k+2`, `s ≥ t+2`,
`E‖A − Â‖_F² ≤ (1 + t/(s−t−1)) (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.
Hypotheses: `hc` (`lem:completion`'s factor with `q = rank(AΩ) ≤ t`), `hcond`
(`lem:completion` + tower property), `hstruct` (`prop:hmt-struct` for
`Y = ‖(I−QQᵀ)A‖_F²`), `hZ` (`lem:moments` + `lem:invmom`, as in the proof of `thm:RSVD`).
The hypothesis `hk` is not used by the arithmetic; it is kept for fidelity.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (uses `rsvd-expected-error`).

name: NLAlib.Assembly.integral_le_sqrt_integral_sq
doc:
Jensen's inequality in the form used throughout Chen–Persson: for a nonnegative
square-integrable random variable `Y`, `E Y ≤ √(E Y²)`. Proved from
`0 ≤ Var Y = E Y² − (E Y)²`. Helper for atlas `rsvd-expected-error` (Frobenius-norm,
unsquared form of HMT 2011, Thm 10.5).

signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.rsvd_assembly.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X Zsq : Ω → ℝ} {OPTsq c : ℝ} (hX : ∀ (ω : Ω), X ω ≤ OPTsq + Zsq ω)
  (hZ : ∫ (ω : Ω), Zsq ω ∂μ = c * OPTsq) (hXi : MeasureTheory.Integrable X μ) (hZi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Zsq μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ (1 + c) * OPTsq
name: NLAlib.Assembly.rsvd_assembly
doc:
Assembly of Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD` (HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case).
* `X = ‖A − Â‖_F²`, `Zsq = ‖Σ₂ Ω₂ Ω₁†‖_F²`, `OPTsq = ‖Σ₂‖_F² = ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.
* `hX` is `prop:hmt-struct` (deterministic; `NLAlib.frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset`).

  `E ‖Σ₂ Ω₂ Ω₁†‖_F² = ‖Σ₂‖_F² · k/(t−k−1)`; here with a general constant `c`.
Atlas `rsvd-expected-error`.

signature:

Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD` (HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case), expectation level,

signature:
NLAlib.ConcaveOn.le_map_integral_of_integral_mem.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω]

doc:
`IsSVD A U V`: `U`, `V` are orthogonal and `A = U Σ Vᵀ` with `Σ = rectDiag (singularValues A)`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3; HMT 2011, §2.1). The `k`-th columns of `U` and `V` are the
left/right singular vectors for `σ_k`. Atlas `svd`.

`A i j = ∑_{k < min m n} σ_k U_{ik} V_{jk}`, i.e. `A = ∑_k σ_k u_k v_kᵀ`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6; HMT 2011, §2.1). Atlas `svd`.

      (transpose_mul_right : V.transpose * V = 1) →

name: NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding
doc:
`S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U`: `(1 - ε)‖Ux‖² ≤ ‖SUx‖² ≤ (1 + ε)‖Ux‖²` for

Basis independence, easy direction: an embedding for `range U` is an embedding for

Atlas: `ose-def`.

Basis independence, converse direction: if `C` has a right inverse `D` (`C D = 1`, so

Atlas: `ose-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs : n → ℝ) : (n → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr
doc:
Expected squared error `E‖x_k - xs‖²` after `k` randomized Kaczmarz steps started at `x`,
rows drawn i.i.d. with probabilities `prob A`. Defined by first-step recursion:
`expErr 0 x = ‖x - xs‖²`, `expErr (k+1) x = ∑ i, prob A i * expErr k (step A b x i)`.
See `expErr_eq_sum_paths` for the path-sum form. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_eq_sum_paths.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k =
    ∑ ω,
      (∏ j, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A (ω j)) * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_eq_sum_paths
doc:
`expErr` is the expectation over i.i.d. row sequences: the sum over all `ω : Fin k → m` of
`(∏ j, prob A (ω j)) * ‖run A b k ω x - xs‖²`. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k ≤ (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz converges linearly in expectation.**
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.
If `A *ᵥ xs = b` and `σ² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖A v‖²` for all `v`, then after `k` steps with rows drawn
i.i.d. with probability `‖A i‖² / ‖A‖_F²`,
`E‖x_k - xs‖² ≤ (1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x₀ - xs‖²`.
Deviations from the printed statement: SV09 take `A` of full column rank and `σ = ‖A⁻¹‖⁻¹`
(rate `1 - κ(A)⁻²`); here `σ` is any constant satisfying `hσ` (the sharp choice is
`σ_min(A)`, atlas `courant-fischer`), and no rank or nonzero-row assumption is needed.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_succ.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x (k + 1) =
    ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i) k
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_succ
doc: Unfolding `expErr` at `k + 1` steps (first-step analysis). Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_zero.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x 0 = (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_zero
doc: Unfolding `expErr` at `0` steps. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (hA : A ≠ 0) :
  ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) =
    (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) - A.mulVec (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x - xs) / NLAlib.frobSq A
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_eq
doc:
One-step expected error identity:
`∑ i, prob A i * ‖step A b x i - xs‖² = ‖x - xs‖² - ‖A (x - xs)‖² / ‖A‖_F²` for `A ≠ 0`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) :
  ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_le
doc:
One-step contraction of randomized Kaczmarz: if `σ² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖A v‖²` for all `v`
(`σ` a lower bound on the smallest singular value, atlas `courant-fischer`), then
`∑ i, prob A i * ‖step A b x i - xs‖² ≤ (1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²) ‖x - xs‖²`.
No hypothesis on `A` (for `A = 0` the left side is `0` and the rate is `1`).
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :

NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.eq_def.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x✝ : ℕ)

    | 0, x, x_1 => x_1
    | k.succ, ω, x => NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k (Fin.tail ω) (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x (ω 0))

containing `xs`): `‖step A b x i - xs‖² = ‖x - xs‖² - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs))² / ‖A i‖²`.
Holds for every row; for a zero row both sides equal `‖x - xs‖²`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Algorithm (eq. (2)); atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:

name: NLAlib.completion_reduction
doc:
**Exact Gaussian completion, deterministic reduction** (Chen–Persson, Lemma
`lem:completion`; Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Thm 5.1).

Fixed `Q` (orthonormal columns, `q ≥ 1`), its orthogonal completion `Qp = Q⊥`
(`QQᵀ + Q⊥Q⊥ᵀ = I`), fixed `A`, random `Ψ` with `s ≥ q + 2`; `G₁ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q`,
`G₂ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q⊥`, `E = residual Q A = (I − QQᵀ)A`.
* `hG₁`: `G₁` has full column rank a.s. (so `G₁†G₁ = I`), the "almost surely" of the paper;
* `hG₂`: `E‖G₁†G₂(Q⊥ᵀE)‖_F² = E‖G₁†‖_F² · ‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F²` — `lem:moments` for `G₂` conditionally
  on `G₁` (independence of `G₁`, `G₂`) followed by the tower property;
* `hG₁m`: `E‖G₁†‖_F² = q/(s−q−1)` — `lem:invmom` (needs `s ≥ q+2`, `q ≥ 1`);
* `hGi`: integrability of the noise term.
Everything else in the paper's proof (`ΨᵀA = G₁QᵀA + G₂Q⊥ᵀE`, `X̂ = QᵀA + G₁†G₂Q⊥ᵀE`,
Pythagoras, `‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F = ‖E‖_F`) is proved in `SketchedRegression.lean` and used here.

`singularValues_antitone`). Atlas `svd`.

`ℝᵐ` (atlas `orthonormal-completion`) giving `U`.

doc:
**Generalized Nyström expected error** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN`; Tropp–Webber 2023,
Thm 5.1). Output `Â ω = sketchedOutput (Q ω) (Ψ ω) A = Q(ΨᵀQ)†ΨᵀA` with `Q ω = orth(AΩ ω)`
having `q` columns, `q ≤ t` (the paper's `q = rank(AΩ)`; here `q` is fixed, the generic case
being `q = t`), `t ≥ k+2`, `s ≥ t+2`.

  the Gaussian moment identity of the proof of `thm:RSVD`);
* `hcond`: `lem:completion` applied conditionally on `Ω` (independence of `Ψ` and `Ω`), then
  the tower property: `E‖A − Â‖_F² = E[(1 + q/(s−q−1)) ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²]`. Its per-`Ω` content
  is `completion_reduction`; see `gn_main_of_completion` for a version whose hypothesis is the
  Gaussian noise moment instead;
* `hYi`, `hZi`: integrability of `‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²` and `‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖_F²`.
Conclusion: `E‖A − Â‖_F² ≤ (1 + t/(s−t−1)) (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.

doc:
**Generalized Nyström with Gaussian sketches** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN`; Tropp–Webber
2023, Thm 5.1). `Ω` (`n × t`) and `Ψ` (`m × s`) independent standard Gaussian matrices,
`t ≥ k + 2`, `s ≥ t + 2`; `Q ω = Qf(Ω ω)` with `q ≤ t` columns, `q ≥ 1`, `Qf` entrywise
measurable, a.s. orthonormal columns and `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)` (the user's choice of
`orth(AΩ)`). Output `Â = Q(ΨᵀQ)†ΨᵀA`:
`E‖A − Â‖_F² ≤ (1 + t/(s−t−1)) (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.
`gn_main` with every Gaussian and integrability hypothesis discharged: `hcond` by Fubini for
independent variables (`lintegral_of_indepFun`) and `completion_gaussian_of_orthonormal` for
each fixed `Ω`; `hYi` from `‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F ≤ ‖A‖_F`.
Deviations: index types are `Fin` (the laws of `Ω` and `Ψ` live on `Fin n → Fin t → ℝ` and

doc:
Second moments of an isotropic vector with pairwise independent coordinates:

signature:

doc:
Fourth mixed moments of a vector with independent, centred coordinates of unit variance and
common fourth moment `m₄`:

Atlas: `hutchinson-variance` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_block_mul_pinvR_block.{u_1} {Ωs : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ωs]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n k r r' t : ℕ} {Ω : Ωs → Fin n → Fin t → ℝ}
  (hΩ : MeasureTheory.Measure.map Ω μ = NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t) (V₁ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ)
  (V₂ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin r') ℝ) (hV₁ : V₁.transpose * V₁ = 1) (hV₂ : V₂.transpose * V₂ = 1)
  (hV₁₂ : V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0) (S₂ : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r') ℝ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (S₂ * (V₂.transpose * Matrix.of (Ω ω)) * NLAlib.pinvR (V₁.transpose * Matrix.of (Ω ω))) ∂μ =
    NLAlib.frobSq S₂ * ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.pinvR (V₁.transpose * Matrix.of (Ω ω))) ∂μ
name: NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_block_mul_pinvR_block
doc:
**RSVD inverse-moment factorisation.** If `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix and
`V₁`, `V₂` have orthonormal, mutually orthogonal columns, then
`E ‖S₂ (V₂ᵀΩ) (V₁ᵀΩ)†‖_F² = ‖S₂‖_F² E ‖(V₁ᵀΩ)†‖_F²` for every fixed `S₂`.

HMT 2011 (Halko–Martinsson–Tropp), proof of Thm 10.5 (conditioning on `Ω₁`, then Prop 10.1).
This is hypothesis `hinv` of `NLAlib.rsvd_truncated_main` modulo the inverse moment
`E ‖Ω₁†‖_F² = k/(t−k−1)`. No integrability hypothesis is needed (see
`integral_frobSq_mul_gaussian_mul_of_indepFun`). `Ω` is array-valued; for a `Matrix`-valued
`Ω'` take `Ω := fun ω => Matrix.of.symm (Ω' ω)` (definitionally `Matrix.of (Ω ω) = Ω' ω`).
Atlas `gaussian-conditioning`.

signature:
NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_gaussianMatrix_mul.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] {p m : ℕ}
  (S : Matrix ι (Fin p) ℝ) (T : Matrix (Fin m) κ ℝ) :
  ∫ (G : Fin p → Fin m → ℝ), NLAlib.frobSq (S * Matrix.of G * T) ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix p m =
    NLAlib.frobSq S * NLAlib.frobSq T
name: NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_gaussianMatrix_mul
doc:
**Second Frobenius moment of a sandwiched Gaussian matrix.** For fixed `S` and `T` and a
`p × m` standard Gaussian matrix `G`, `E ‖S G T‖_F² = ‖S‖_F² ‖T‖_F²`.

HMT 2011 (Halko–Martinsson–Tropp), Prop 10.1, first identity (`E‖SGT‖_F² = ‖S‖_F² ‖T‖_F²`).
Atlas: `gaussian-frob-second-moment`. The outer dimensions are arbitrary finite index types
(the source and the Prove2me statement use `Fin a`, `Fin n`). Ported from the Prove2me
workspace, Gaussian Random Matrices series.

name: NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_gaussian_mul_of_indepFun
doc:
**Sandwiched Gaussian second moment, conditioned.** If `Y` is a standard Gaussian
`p × m` matrix independent of `X`, then `E ‖S Y T(X)‖_F² = ‖S‖_F² E ‖T(X)‖_F²`.

No integrability hypothesis: both integrands are nonnegative and the identity holds for the
lower Lebesgue integrals (`lintegral_frobSq_mul_gaussian_mul_of_indepFun`); when the right side
is not integrable both Bochner integrals are `0`. Integrability of the left side is
`integrable_frobSq_mul_gaussian_mul_of_indepFun`.
HMT 2011 Prop 10.1 with the tower property (proof of Thm 10.5). Atlas `gaussian-conditioning`.
Measurability of `T` is stated entrywise (`Matrix` carries no `MeasurableSpace` instance).

doc:
**Completion-step inverse-moment factorisation** (transposed form of
`integral_frobSq_mul_block_mul_pinvR_block`). If `Ψ` is an `m × s` standard Gaussian matrix and

the conditioning argument of HMT 2011 Thm 10.5 applied to the transposed sketch. Here
`(ΨᵀQ)† = pinvL (ΨᵀQ)`. Atlas `gaussian-conditioning`.

signature:

matrix this closes hypothesis `hinv` of `NLAlib.rsvd_truncated_main`. HMT 2011 §10.2 (block law).

first component).

signature:
NLAlib.integral_quadForm_eq_trace.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {Ω : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {z : Ω → n → ℝ}
  (hz : ∀ (i : n), MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun ω => z ω i) 2 μ)
  (hind : ∀ (i j : n), i ≠ j → ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (fun ω => z ω i) (fun ω => z ω j) μ)
  (hmean : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ∂μ = 0) (hsq : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) :

name: NLAlib.integral_quadForm_eq_trace
doc:
**Hutchinson's estimator is unbiased.** If the coordinates `z_i` of a random vector are
square-integrable, pairwise independent, centred and have unit second moment, then
`𝔼[zᵀ A z] = tr A`.
Source: Hutchinson (1989) [`hutch89`]; Avron–Toledo (2011) [`at11`].
Atlas: `hutchinson-unbiased`.
Deviation: stated for any isotropic vector with pairwise independent coordinates (only
`𝔼[z_i z_j] = δ_ij` is used); the source states it for Rademacher `z`.

  (hsq : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) (h4 : ∀ (i : n), MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => z ω i ^ 4) μ)
  {m₄ : ℝ} (hm4 : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 4 ∂μ = m₄) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.quadForm A (z ω) ^ 2 ∂μ =
    A.trace ^ 2 + ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j ^ 2 + ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j * A j i + (m₄ - 3) * ∑ i, A i i ^ 2

doc:
Second moment of Hutchinson's estimator: for a random vector with independent, centred
coordinates of unit variance and common fourth moment `m₄`,
`𝔼[(zᵀ A z)²] = (tr A)² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij A_ji + (m₄ − 3) ∑ᵢ A_ii²`.

Atlas: `hutchinson-variance`.

semidefinite, `‖V‖ = max ‖V₁‖ ‖V₂‖`, and `intdim V` lies between `min (intdim V₁) (intdim V₂)` and

Orthonormal form of a subspace embedding (Woodruff 2014 §2.1; Martinsson–Tropp 2020 §8.7):
for `U` with orthonormal columns, `S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U` iff
`(1 - ε)‖x‖² ≤ ‖SUx‖² ≤ (1 + ε)‖x‖²` for every coefficient vector `x`.

Atlas: `ose-def`.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_mul_right_iff

embedding for `range U` iff it is one for `range (U C)`. The property depends on the subspace
only.

Atlas: `ose-def`.

direction used in practice: for `U` with orthonormal columns, `‖(SU)ᵀ(SU) − I‖₂ ≤ ε` implies
that `S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U`. (The converse also holds; not yet
formalized.)

Atlas: `ose-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_distributional (k n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G | |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec x - x ⬝ᵥ x| > ε * x ⬝ᵥ x} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)))
name: NLAlib.jl_distributional
doc:
SCAFFOLD: jl-distributional.

Distributional Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma for the Gaussian sketch (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003,
Lem 2.2; Woodruff 2014 §2.1): for `S = k^{-1/2} G` with `G` standard Gaussian `k × n`, any fixed
`x : ℝⁿ` and `0 < ε < 1`,
`P[|‖Sx‖² − ‖x‖²| > ε‖x‖²] ≤ 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Deferred: the proof needs rotation invariance of the Gaussian matrix (`‖Gx‖² / ‖x‖²` is
`χ²_k`) and the two Chernoff tails of the chi-square law (atlas `rotation-invariance`,
`chi-square-upper-tail`, `chi-square-lower-tail`), none of which is yet in the library.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (↑N ^ 2 * 2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)))
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, union-bound form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for a finite
family `p : Fin N → ℝⁿ`, the probability that the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` distorts some
pairwise squared distance `‖p i − p j‖²` by more than a factor `1 ± ε` is at most
`N² · 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Deviation: the union is taken over all `N²` ordered pairs (not the `N(N−1)/2` unordered ones),
which costs a constant factor `2` in the bound. No measurability hypothesis is needed (the union
bound holds for the outer measure).

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)

  ∃ S,
    ∀ (i j : Fin N),
      (1 - ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j) ≤ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ∧
        S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ≤ (1 + ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)

doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, existence form (Johnson–Lindenstrauss 1984; Dasgupta–Gupta
2003, Thm 2.1): any `N ≥ 2` points of `ℝⁿ` admit a linear map `S : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ` with
`k ≥ 48 log N / ε²` that preserves every pairwise squared distance to within `1 ± ε`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -

              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 2)

doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, `O(ε⁻² log N)` form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for
`N ≥ 2` points, `0 < ε < 1` and `k ≥ 48 log N / ε²`, the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G`

at failure probability `1 − 1/N`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε δ : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)

doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma with explicit dimension (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): if
`0 < ε < 1`, `0 < δ` and `k ≥ (ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ log(2N²/δ)`, then with probability at least

in `jl_lemma`.

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_bernstein.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m n N : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero n] (S : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ)
  (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (S k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun S μ)
  (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), S k ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.spectralNorm (S k ω) ≤ L) :
  have Z := fun ω => ∑ k, S k ω;
  have v := NLAlib.rectSecondMoment μ Z;
  v =
      max (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), S k ω * (S k ω).conjTranspose ∂μ))
        (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), (S k ω).conjTranspose * S k ω ∂μ)) ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω) ∂μ ≤ √(2 * v * Real.log (↑m + ↑n)) + L * Real.log (↑m + ↑n) / 3 ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → (μ {ω | t ≤ NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.bernsteinTail (m + n) v L t
name: NLAlib.matrix_bernstein
doc:
Matrix Bernstein inequality, rectangular case: for an independent sum `Z` of centered random `m ×
n` matrices with `‖S k‖ ≤ L`, `𝔼 ‖Z‖ ≤ √(2 v log (m + n)) + L log (m + n) / 3` and `P{‖Z‖ ≥ t} ≤
bernsteinTail (m + n) v L t`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 6.1.1. Atlas: `matrix-bernstein`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_chernoff.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L : ℝ)
  (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (X k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hHerm : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X k ω).IsHermitian)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, 0 ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMin (X k ω) ∧ NLAlib.lambdaMax (X k ω) ≤ L) :
  have Y := fun ω => ∑ k, X k ω;
  have a := NLAlib.lambdaMin (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ);
  have b := NLAlib.lambdaMax (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ);
  a = NLAlib.lambdaMin (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ) ∧
    b = NLAlib.lambdaMax (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ) ∧
      (∀ (θ : ℝ),
          0 < θ →
            (1 - Real.exp (-θ)) / θ * a - L * Real.log ↑d / θ ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMin (Y ω) ∂μ ∧
              ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω) ∂μ ≤ (Real.exp θ - 1) / θ * b + L * Real.log ↑d / θ) ∧
        (∀ (ε : ℝ),
            0 ≤ ε → ε < 1 → (μ {ω | NLAlib.lambdaMin (Y ω) ≤ (1 - ε) * a}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail d a L ε) ∧
          ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → (μ {ω | (1 + ε) * b ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail d b L ε
name: NLAlib.matrix_chernoff
doc:
Matrix Chernoff inequality: for an independent sum of random positive semidefinite matrices with
`λmax ≤ L`, expectation bounds on `λmin` and `λmax` for every `θ > 0` and the lower and upper
tails `chernoffLowerTail`, `chernoffUpperTail`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 5.1.1, eqs (5.1.1–6). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`. Ported from the Prove2me mission
*An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 5*.

The expectation bounds are stated for every `θ > 0` before optimisation; degenerate `L = 0`
follows the piecewise tail definitions.

signature:

  (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (g k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun g μ)
  (hLaw : (∀ (k : Fin N), NLAlib.IsStandardGaussian μ (g k)) ∨ ∀ (k : Fin N), NLAlib.IsRademacher μ (g k)) :
  have Z := fun ω => ∑ k, g k ω • B k;
  have v := NLAlib.rectSecondMoment μ Z;
  v =
      max (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, B k * (B k).conjTranspose))
        (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, (B k).conjTranspose * B k)) ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω) ∂μ ≤ √(2 * v * Real.log (↑m + ↑n)) ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → (μ {ω | t ≤ NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.gaussianSeriesTail (m + n) v t

doc:

the maximum of the two row/column sums, `𝔼 ‖Z‖ ≤ √(2 v log (m + n))`, and `P{‖Z‖ ≥ t} ≤
gaussianSeriesTail (m + n) v t`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 4.1.1. Atlas: `matrix-gaussian-series`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An

  (hZi :

name: NLAlib.rsvd_main
doc:
**Randomized SVD** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD` for Algorithm RSVD, untruncated output
`Q QᵀA`; HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case).

Same hypotheses as `rsvd_truncated_main` except that no truncation `Y` is needed: the proof
goes through the second inequality of `prop:hmt-struct`
(`frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset`, i.e.
`‖A − QQᵀA‖_F ≤ ‖A − QB‖_F` for every `B`, applied to `B = QᵀZ`), the untruncated analogue
of the argument for `Q⟦QᵀA⟧ₖ`. (Equivalently, `frobSq (A − Q(QᵀA)) ≤ frobSq (A − QY)` for
the truncated output, see `frobSq_sub_mul_transpose_mul_le_frobSq_sub_mul`.)
Conclusion: `E‖A − QQᵀA‖_F² ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.
Atlas `rsvd-expected-error`.

name: NLAlib.rsvd_main_gaussian
doc:
**Randomized SVD with a Gaussian test matrix** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD`, Algorithm
RSVD; HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case): if `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix,
`t ≥ k + 2`, and `Q ω` has a.s. orthonormal columns with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then
`E‖A − QQᵀA‖_F² ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²` (`‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F² = frobSq S₂` via the block SVD).
`rsvd_main` with its Gaussian hypotheses `hunit`, `hinv`, `hZi` discharged. The integrability
hypothesis `hXi` is also removed: when the error is not integrable its Bochner integral is `0`
and the (nonnegative) bound holds trivially. No measurability of `Q` is required.
Deviation: `n`, `k`, `r`, `r'`, `t` are `Fin` (the Gaussian law of `Ω` and the block lemmas of
`Gaussian/Conditioning.lean` live on `Fin`); the row type `m` and the column type `q` of `Q`
are arbitrary.
Atlas `rsvd-expected-error` (uses `gaussian-conditioning`, `pinv-frob-moment`,
`gaussian-full-rank-ae`, `hmt-9-1-frobenius`).

signature:
NLAlib.sum_fourth_moment_contraction.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (m₄ : ℝ) :
  ∑ i,
      ∑ j,
        ∑ k,
          ∑ l,
            A i j * A k l *
              (((((if i = j then 1 else 0) * if k = l then 1 else 0) +
                    (if i = k then 1 else 0) * if j = l then 1 else 0) +
                  (if i = l then 1 else 0) * if j = k then 1 else 0) +
                (m₄ - 3) * (((if i = j then 1 else 0) * if i = k then 1 else 0) * if i = l then 1 else 0)) =
    A.trace ^ 2 + ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j ^ 2 + ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j * A j i + (m₄ - 3) * ∑ i, A i i ^ 2
name: NLAlib.sum_fourth_moment_contraction
doc:
The index sum behind the Hutchinson variance:
`∑ᵢⱼₖₗ A_ij A_kl (δ_ij δ_kl + δ_ik δ_jl + δ_il δ_jk + (m₄ − 3) δ_ijkl)
  = (tr A)² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij A_ji + (m₄ − 3) ∑ᵢ A_ii²`.
Atlas: `hutchinson-variance` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.variance_quadForm.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {Ω : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  {z : Ω → n → ℝ} (hmeas : ∀ (i : n), AEMeasurable (fun ω => z ω i) μ)
  (hindep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i ω => z ω i) μ) (hmean : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ∂μ = 0)
  (hsq : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) (h4 : ∀ (i : n), MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => z ω i ^ 4) μ)
  {m₄ : ℝ} (hm4 : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 4 ∂μ = m₄) :
  ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun ω => NLAlib.quadForm A (z ω)) μ =
    ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j ^ 2 + ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j * A j i + (m₄ - 3) * ∑ i, A i i ^ 2
name: NLAlib.variance_quadForm
doc:
**Variance of Hutchinson's estimator** (general form). If the coordinates of `z` are
independent, centred, of unit variance and common fourth moment `m₄ = 𝔼[z_i⁴]`, then
`Var[zᵀ A z] = ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij A_ji + (m₄ − 3) ∑ᵢ A_ii²` (mathematically the same as
`∑_{i≠j} (A_ij² + A_ij A_ji) + (m₄ − 1) ∑ᵢ A_ii²`; that form is not stated separately).
Source: Hutchinson (1989) [`hutch89`] (Rademacher case); Avron–Toledo (2011) [`at11`],
Lem 5 (Gaussian), Lem 6 (Rademacher). Atlas: `hutchinson-variance`.
Deviation: no symmetry of `A` assumed; general fourth moment `m₄` (`m₄ = 1` Rademacher,
`m₄ = 3` Gaussian).

signature:
NLAlib.variance_quadForm_of_isSymm.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {Ω : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsSymm) {z : Ω → n → ℝ} (hmeas : ∀ (i : n), AEMeasurable (fun ω => z ω i) μ)
  (hindep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i ω => z ω i) μ) (hmean : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ∂μ = 0)
  (hsq : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) (h4 : ∀ (i : n), MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => z ω i ^ 4) μ)
  {m₄ : ℝ} (hm4 : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 4 ∂μ = m₄) :
  ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun ω => NLAlib.quadForm A (z ω)) μ =
    2 * (NLAlib.frobSq A - ∑ i, A i i ^ 2) + (m₄ - 1) * ∑ i, A i i ^ 2
name: NLAlib.variance_quadForm_of_isSymm
doc:
**Variance of Hutchinson's estimator, symmetric `A`.**
`Var[zᵀ A z] = 2‖A‖_F² + (m₄ − 3) ∑ᵢ A_ii² = 2(‖A‖_F² − ∑ᵢ A_ii²) + (m₄ − 1) ∑ᵢ A_ii²`.
Source: Avron–Toledo (2011) [`at11`], Lem 5, 6; Hutchinson (1989) [`hutch89`].
Atlas: `hutchinson-variance`.

  (hm4 : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 4 ∂μ = 1) :
